content: Trends is a collection of scientific journals owned by Elsevier, focusing on publishing review articles across various fields of biology. These journals are currently part of Elsevier's Cell Press group. The Trends series was initiated in 1976 with the launch of Trends in Biochemical Sciences (TIBS). This was soon followed by the introduction of Trends in Neurosciences (TINS), Trends in Pharmacological Sciences (TIPS), and Immunology Today. During the 1980s and 1990s, the series expanded significantly, even including non-biological titles such as Trends in Food Science and Technology and Trends in Polymer Science. However, these non-biological titles were later discontinued or removed from the series. In 2001, Drug Discovery Today was spun off as an independent brand. Initially published in Cambridge, UK, the editorial office of Trends moved to London in the mid-1990s after Elsevier acquired Pergamon Press. The current lineup of Trends journals includes the following: Trends in Biochemical Sciences (TIBS), focusing on biochemistry, established in 1976. Trends in Biotechnology, covering biotechnology, launched in 1983. Trends in Cell Biology, dedicated to cell biology, introduced in 1991. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, addressing cognitive science, started in 1997. Trends in Ecology & Evolution (TREE), focusing on evolutionary ecology, initiated in 1986. Trends in Endocrinology and Metabolism, covering endocrinology and metabolism, launched in 1990. Trends in Genetics (TIG), focusing on genetics, established in 1985. Trends in Immunology, dedicated to immunology, started in 1980 (formerly known as Immunology Today). Trends in Microbiology (TIM), covering microbiology, introduced in 1993. Trends in Molecular Medicine, focusing on molecular medicine, launched in 1995 (formerly known as Molecular Medicine Today). Trends in Neurosciences (TINS), addressing neuroscience, established in 1978. Trends in Parasitology, focusing on parasitology, started in 1985 (formerly known as Parasitology Today). Trends in Pharmacological Sciences (TIPS), covering pharmacology, launched in 1979. Trends in Plant Science, dedicated to botany, introduced in 1996. All of these journals are published on a monthly basis, with the exception of Trends in Endocrinology and Metabolism, which releases ten issues per year.
